## Overview

::: {.callout-important}
## Welcome to DataLab!
Today you'll rotate through 6 stations, generating the dataset we'll analyse throughout the term. Your data will become our teaching examples for distributions, t-tests, correlations, and more.
:::

## The Session Structure

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 0:00-0:15 | Welcome, collect participant ID, complete Part 1 of survey |
| 0:15-1:45 | Rotate through 6 stations (~12-15 min each) |
| 1:45-1:55 | Complete Part 2 of survey |
| 1:55-2:00 | Debrief and wrap-up |

## Before You Start

1. **Collect your participant card** from the instructors
2. **Note your group colour** - this is your rotation group
3. **Scan the QR code** and complete Part 1 of the Qualtrics survey
4. **Wait at your starting station** until instructed to begin

::: {.callout-note}
## Part 1 Survey (Complete First!)
Before the stations begin, you'll complete:

- Consent form
- Basic information (sleep, lifestyle)
- A brief personality questionnaire
- How you're feeling right now
:::

## Station 1: Reflex Test {#station-1}

![](images/station1-reflex.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**How fast is your nervous system?**

At this station, you'll measure your **reaction time** using a simple ruler-drop task.

### What You'll Do

1. **Partner A** holds the ruler at the 30cm mark, letting it hang vertically
2. **Partner B** positions thumb and finger at the 0cm mark — don't touch the ruler!
3. Partner A drops the ruler **without warning** (within 5 seconds)
4. Partner B catches it **as fast as possible**
5. Read the cm mark at the **top of your thumb**
6. Complete **5 trials**, then swap roles

### What You'll Record

- Which hand you used (dominant or non-dominant)
- The distance caught on each trial (in cm)
- Any trials you missed

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Science
Your catch distance can be converted to reaction time using physics! The formula involves the distance fallen and gravitational acceleration. You'll see this conversion in the data.
:::

---

## Station 2: Mind Palace {#station-2}

![](images/station2-mind-palace.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**What survives the interference?**

This station tests your **working memory** and the effects of distraction.

### What You'll Do

1. **STUDY (30 sec)**: Look at the word list card and try to memorise all 10 words
2. **DISTRACT (60 sec)**: Turn the card face-down. Complete the maths problems.
3. **RECALL (90 sec)**: Write down as many words as you remember
4. **SCORE**: Check your answers and count correct words

### What You'll Record

- Total words correctly recalled (out of 10)
- Which positions (1-10) you remembered
- Any "intrusions" (words you wrote that weren't on the list)
- What strategy (if any) you used

::: {.callout-warning}
## No Peeking!
Keep the word list face-down during the distraction and recall phases. The maths problems are meant to be distracting — work quickly, don't worry about accuracy.
:::

---

## Station 3: Time Warp {#station-3}

![](images/station3-time-warp.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**Your brain's internal clock**

This station explores how accurately you perceive time and physical dimensions.

### Task A: 60-Second Estimation

1. Close your eyes or look down
2. When you hear "Start", begin sensing time passing
3. Say "Stop" when you believe exactly **60 seconds** have passed
4. The facilitator will record your actual time

::: {.callout-tip}
## Try Not to Count!
The most interesting data comes when you try to *feel* the time passing rather than counting "one Mississippi, two Mississippi..."
:::

### Task B: Visual Estimation (Lines)

1. Look at **Line Card A**
2. Estimate its length in centimetres (don't measure!)
3. Repeat with **Line Card B**

### Task C: Tactile Estimation (Strings)

1. Feel **String 1** without looking (eyes closed)
2. Estimate its length in centimetres
3. Repeat with **String 2**

### What You'll Record

- Your 60-second time estimate
- Your estimates for both lines (cm)
- Your estimates for both strings (cm)
- Whether you counted during the time estimation

---

## Station 4: Sixth Sense {#station-4}

![](images/station4-sixth-sense.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**Can you tell when someone is watching you?**

This station investigates whether humans can detect when they're being stared at.

### What You'll Do

1. Sit **back-to-back** with your partner, about 1 metre apart
2. **STARER**: Flip the coin to decide
   - Heads = Stare at partner's head
   - Tails = Look away
3. Hold your position for **15 seconds**
4. **TARGET**: Say "Staring" or "Not staring"
5. Rate your **confidence** (1 = pure guess, 5 = certain)
6. Complete **6 trials** as target, then swap roles

### What You'll Record

- For each trial: What actually happened, what you guessed, your confidence
- Your total correct out of 6

::: {.callout-note}
## Solo Participants
If you don't have a partner, there's a video version available — ask the facilitator.
:::

---

## Station 5: Lady Luck {#station-5}

![](images/station5-lady-luck.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**How random can you be?**

This station explores human intuitions about randomness.

### Task A: Random Number Generation

Generate **20 "random" numbers** between 1 and 10. Say each aloud as it comes to mind — don't plan ahead!

::: {.callout-tip}
## Be Spontaneous!
Just say the first number that pops into your head. Don't try to make it "look" random.
:::

### Task B: Dice Rolling

1. **First**: Predict whether you'll roll more 6s than expected by chance
2. Roll the die **10 times** and record each outcome

### Task C: Coin Flipping

1. Flip the coin **10 times** and record each outcome (H or T)
2. Note the longest run of the same outcome in a row

### What You'll Record

- All 20 random numbers you generated
- Your prediction about dice 6s
- All 10 dice outcomes
- All 10 coin flip outcomes
- Longest consecutive run

---

## Station 6: Frontal Lob {#station-6}

![](images/station6-frontal-lob.png){.station-img fig-align="center"}

**Precision meets confidence**

This station examines the relationship between your **self-assessment** and **actual performance**.

### What You'll Do

1. **Before throwing**: Rate your throwing ability on a scale of 1-10
2. Stand at the marked line
3. Throw ping pong balls into the basket
4. Complete **10 throws** with your dominant hand
5. Count your successes
6. *Optional*: 5 throws with your non-dominant hand

### What You'll Record

- Your self-rating (1-10)
- Number of successful throws (out of 10)
- Non-dominant hand successes (if attempted)
- Which is your dominant hand

::: {.callout-note}
## Metacognition
How well does your self-rating match your actual performance? This is called **calibration** — and most people aren't very well calibrated!
:::

---

## After the Stations

### Complete Part 2 of the Survey

Once all rotations are complete, return to the survey to answer:

- How you're feeling **now** (so we can compare to before)
- Which station was your favourite/least favourite
- Any feedback or comments

::: {.callout-important}
## Pre-Post Design
By measuring your mood before AND after DataLab, we can analyse whether participation affected how you feel. This is a **within-subjects** design — you'll learn more about this soon!
:::

### Form Your Project Groups

By the end of the session, form groups of **3-4 students**.

Your group will:

- Work together on the group research project
- Conduct labs together from Week 16
- Generate data for the Research Report (Week 22)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tips for Group Formation
- Choose people you can reliably meet with outside class
- Consider different strengths (organisation, analysis, writing)
- Exchange contact details before leaving
:::

## What We Did Today
1. Generated data as both participants and testers
2. Experienced variability in human performance
3. Measured multiple psychological constructs:
   - Reaction time, memory, time perception
   - Sensory detection, randomness intuition, metacognition
4. Created a pre-post design to measure mood change
5. Formed project groups for the term
